title: SAC: Disaggregated KV Cache System for Sparse Attention LLMs with CXL
event_hint: SAC (arXiv 2606.19746v1) is presented as the first CXL-based disaggregated KV cache system for sparse-attention LLMs, fetching only the dynamically selected top-k KV entries on demand at cache-line granularity via CXL load/store, instead of RDMA full-prefix fetch.
problem: RDMA-based disaggregated KV cache systems fetch the entire prefix KV cache into local memory before decoding (coarse-grained). For sparse-attention models where only a small top-k subset of KV is active per layer, this causes two problems: (P1) transmission bottleneck over RDMA, and (P2) local memory wasting, since the bulk of the fetched KV is never used during decode yet must be held locally, forcing TB-level local memory for high concurrency.
mechanism: SAC keeps the full KV cache in a disaggregated CXL memory pool (multiple CXL-MEM devices behind a CXL switch, host GPUs on PCIe 5.0 x16 / 64 GB/s links). The decode instance (built on the HiSparse framework in SGLang) computes the per-layer top-k selection at runtime and, during each attention layer, directly fetches only those top-k KV entries from the CXL pool into GPU HBM using CXL cache-line-granularity load/store semantics with near-DRAM latency; newly generated token KV is written back to the CXL pool. Three components: a Prefill Instance (writes full KV to the pool), a Decode Instance (on-demand top-k fetch), and a CXL-based KV cache manager exposing a global CXL address space with optimized read/write kernels and device interleaving. The HiSparse device_buffer_size (4K vs 6K) controls the GPU HBM hot-KV cache capacity and thus the CXL fetch volume.

evidence.claim: On DeepSeek-V3.2 (AWQ 4-bit quantization) served via SGLang+HiSparse on an 8xH20 GPU server with a 2TB CXL memory pool, SAC achieves on average 2.1x higher throughput, 9.7x lower TTFT, and 1.8x lower TBT than an RDMA-based memory pool. These are Round-2 (cache-hit / decode-only) results; RDMA's high TTFT stems from transmission-bandwidth saturation under client concurrency and its 1.8x TBT from PCIe bus contention between KV traffic and the HiSparse swap-in process.
evidence.value: 2.1x throughput / 9.7x lower TTFT / 1.8x lower TBT vs RDMA pool
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 AWQ 4-bit; 8xH20 server; 2TB CXL pool; SGLang + HiSparse; Round-2 (cache hit), 512 ShareGPT requests, concurrency 64, context 16K-128K, output 1K tokens; confirmed in Evaluation Sec 5.1
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 7, Sec 5.1 (End-to-End Performance Comparison), Figures 9-10

evidence.claim: Against a local-host-DRAM upper bound on the same workload, SAC achieves throughput within 91% of the DRAM baseline (i.e. ~9% degradation) on average, with only marginal TBT and TTFT increases, supporting the near-optimal claim for CXL disaggregation.
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 AWQ 4-bit; 8xH20; Round-1 + Round-2; confirmed in Evaluation Sec 5.1

evidence.claim: Sparse KV retrieval-latency microbenchmark (DRAM vs CXL vs RDMA): at 2048 fetched KV indices CXL is ~1.63x DRAM while RDMA is ~19.7x DRAM, with the RDMA/DRAM gap widening as the fetched-index count grows (3.97x at 64 indices up to 19.7x at 2048).
evidence.value: CXL ~1.63x / RDMA ~19.7x relative to DRAM at 2048 indices
evidence.condition: Per-index sparse KV read latency microbenchmark; absolute latency values not given in the figure
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 4, Figure 5 (Retrieval latency comparison for sparse KV)

evidence.claim: KV cache footprint and utilization for DeepSeek-V3.2 (ShareGPT, 1K-token output): per-request footprint is 1.2/2.3/4.6/9.2 GB at 16K/32K/64K/128K context, and at 128K only ~21% of the KV cache is actually utilized, quantifying the local-memory-wasting problem.
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2; ShareGPT dataset; 1K-token output; profiling of active vs inactive KV
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 4, Figure 4 (KV cache usage and footprint for DeepSeek-V3.2)

evidence.claim: RDMA prefix-KV prefetch latency under a 100 Gbps RNIC grows near-linearly with concurrency and context length, reaching dozens of seconds in high-concurrency scenarios and directly inflating TTFT.
evidence.value: dozens of seconds at high concurrency
evidence.condition: Average KV-cache transmission latency across concurrency 1-32 and contexts 16K-128K
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 4, Figure 3 (RDMA prefetch latency for prefix KV cache)

evaluation_context: Model: DeepSeek-V3.2 (AWQ 4-bit quantization; native sparse attention, DSA, top-k=2048 KV latent vectors). Hardware: 8xH20 GPU server with a 2TB CXL memory pool as KV cache backend. Serving stack: SGLang integrated with the HiSparse framework. Workload: 512 requests sampled from ShareGPT; context lengths swept 16K-128K; output length fixed at 1K tokens. Two-round setup: Round-1 (Cache Populate, prefill instance, concurrency 8) and Round-2 (Cache Hit, decode instance, prefill bypassed, concurrency 64). Baselines: RDMA-based memory pool and local host DRAM as upper bound. Headline 2.1x/9.7x/1.8x are Round-2 (decode) results; SAC reaches ~91% of DRAM throughput. Device-interleaving across CXL devices mitigates link contention and the HiSparse device_buffer_size (6K vs 4K) yields ~10.4% higher average throughput via a lower KV miss rate. The exact CXL device count, per-device CXL latency, and the specific RDMA baseline implementation/RNIC model are still not named in the read sections.
limitations: Applicability is restricted to sparse-attention models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.1, DeepSeek-V4 cited); dense-attention models are out of scope (existing CXL work Beluga/TRACT does full-prefix prefetch for dense models). Top-k is fixed at 2048 in the current DSA implementation. The 3x throughput / 256-concurrency / 8xH200 GLM-5.1-FP8 result in Appendix C is HiSparse's prior-work basis, not SAC's own end-to-end result. The headline numbers are now validated in the detailed Evaluation (Sec 5.1) with hardware (8xH20, 2TB CXL pool, AWQ 4-bit) and concurrency (Round-1=8, Round-2=64) known; however the exact CXL device count/per-device latency, the named RDMA baseline (MoonCake/LMCache/RNIC model), and Appendix A setup details remain unread. Source is an arXiv preprint (v1, 2026-06-18).
project_relevance: Directly addresses the topic's memory-semantics question: SAC demonstrates that CXL cache-line-granularity load/store (vs RDMA message-passing) changes remote memory placement/sharing semantics enough to enable fine-grained, on-demand sparse KV access. It also shows end-to-end propagation of a memory-tier change to LLM serving metrics (throughput, TTFT, TBT on SGLang + DeepSeek-V3.2), which is exactly the 'does the benefit reach end-to-end' question on the project card. Note: the offload here is GPU<->CXL-memory data movement via CXL, not Intel DSA/IAA device offload, so it informs the CXL/disaggregated-memory half of the topic rather than the DSA/IAA卸载 half.
source_notes: Source: arXiv 2606.19746v1, FETCHED, source_level A, discovery_source arXiv, published 2026-06-18.
